# Which RFC obsoletes RFC 2616 (HTTP/1.1), and when

**Date:** 2026-11-04
**Question:** Which RFC currently obsoletes RFC 2616 (the HTTP/1.1 specification), and in what year was it published?

## Executive summary

- RFC 2616 (June 1999) was obsoleted by RFC 7230, published June 2014. RFC 7230's header carries the line "Obsoletes: 2145, 2616".
- RFC 2616 was replaced as a set by RFCs 7230–7235 (2014). The RFC 2616 page itself says "This RFC is now obsolete, see" and lists 7230–7235.
- RFC 7230–7235 are themselves superseded. RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics) and RFC 9112 (HTTP/1.1) were published in 2022 and obsolete parts of that set.
- Direct answer for a changelog: RFC 7230 (2014) is the RFC whose header names RFC 2616 as obsolete. The current HTTP/1.1 spec is RFC 9112 (2022), with RFC 9110 (2022) as the companion semantics document.

## Findings

### RFC 2616 status
- RFC 2616 is dated June 1999, Draft Standard / Standards Track. Its page notes it is obsolete and lists RFC 7230, 7231, 7232, 7233, 7234, and 7235 as replacements. [https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc2616] (1999; obsolescence notice reflects 2014)

### RFC 7230 obsoletes RFC 2616
- RFC 7230 is dated June 2014. Its header reads "Obsoletes: 2145, 2616". [https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7230] (2014)
- Caveat: the header block shows no "Obsoleted by" line. The page's banner says "This RFC is now obsolete, see" and lists RFC 9110 and RFC 9112. [https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7230] (2014; banner reflects 2022)

### Current successors (2022)
- RFC 9112 (HTTP/1.1 message syntax and routing) is dated 2022 by its copyright notice. Its abstract says "This document obsoletes portions of RFC 7230." [https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9112] (2022)
- RFC 9110 (HTTP Semantics) is dated 2022 by its copyright notice. Its abstract says it "updates RFC 3864 and obsoletes RFCs 2818, 7231, 7232, 7233, 7235, 7538, 7615, 7694, and portions of 7230." [https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110] (2022)
- Together, RFC 9110 and RFC 9112 are the current HTTP/1.1 specification. RFC 9110 does not list RFC 2616 directly; the chain runs 2616 → 7230 → 9112 (in part).

### Publication-date notes
- The RFC 9110 and RFC 9112 pages gave only the copyright year, not a month. The 2022 year is consistent across both pages.

## Evidence gaps and uncertainties

- "Currently obsoletes" is ambiguous. Read strictly, the RFC whose Obsoletes field names 2616 is RFC 7230 (2014). Read as "the current spec that replaces it", the answer is RFC 9110/9112 (2022). Pick the wording that fits the changelog.
- RFC 9112 obsoletes only "portions" of RFC 7230, so RFC 7230 is not fully retired. Whether 2616 is fully superseded by 9112 alone was not checked clause by clause.
- Only the first 100,000 characters of each RFC page were read. The header and abstract fields were captured; the body was not reviewed.
- The RFC 9110 and RFC 9112 pages did not give a publication month.

## Paywalled must-reads

None. All sources are free IETF/RFC Editor pages.
